dialog.discard.body: What you typed in this dialog will be lost.
dialog.discard.title: Discard your changes?
dialog.guide.gitflow_finish.step1: Finish merges the branch into the branches it goes back to.
dialog.guide.gitflow_finish.step2: A release or hotfix is tagged where it lands on the production branch.
dialog.guide.gitflow_finish.step3: The branch is deleted afterwards, unless you keep it.
dialog.guide.gitflow_finish.step4: Push the branches and the tag to share them.
dialog.guide.gitflow_start.step1: Git Flow keeps released work on the production branch and ongoing work on the development branch.
dialog.guide.gitflow_start.step2: Start creates a branch named with the kind's prefix from its base branch, and checks it out.
dialog.guide.gitflow_start.step3: Commit your work there as usual.
dialog.guide.gitflow_start.step4: Finish merges it back when it is done.
dialog.guide.heading: How it works
dialog.guide.mainline.step1: A merge commit has more than one parent, so what it changed depends on which parent it is compared with.
dialog.guide.mainline.step2: The mainline is the parent the changes are counted against: usually the first, the branch that was merged into.
dialog.guide.mainline.step3: The cherry-pick or revert then uses the changes the other side brought in.
dialog.guide.patch_apply.step1: A patch file is a set of changes written out as text, sometimes with whole commits.
dialog.guide.patch_apply.step2: Applying the changes edits your files as if you had made them; nothing is committed.
dialog.guide.patch_apply.step3: Applying as commits makes each commit again on the current branch, with its message and author.
dialog.guide.patch_apply.step4: Parts that don't fit can be merged three-way or left in .rej files to finish by hand.
dialog.guide.patch_save.step1: A patch file writes your uncommitted changes out as text.
dialog.guide.patch_save.step2: Choose what goes in: all changes, only staged or only unstaged ones, and new files.
dialog.guide.patch_save.step3: Your files and the index are left as they are.
dialog.guide.patch_save.step4: The file can be applied elsewhere with Apply patch or git apply.
dialog.guide.submodule_add.step1: A submodule is another repository kept inside this one, pinned to one commit.
dialog.guide.submodule_add.step2: Glowfly clones the URL into the folder and records it in .gitmodules.
dialog.guide.submodule_add.step3: The folder and .gitmodules are staged; commit them to add the submodule for everyone.
dialog.guide.submodule_add.step4: After pulling, others use Update all submodules to get its files.
dialog.guide.submodule_edit.step1: A submodule's URL and branch are kept in .gitmodules, which is committed with the project.
dialog.guide.submodule_edit.step2: Save writes the change there, to this repository's config, and to the submodule's origin when it is checked out.
dialog.guide.submodule_edit.step3: The branch is used only when a submodule is updated to its remote's latest commit.
dialog.guide.submodule_remove.step1: The submodule's files are removed and it leaves this repository's config.
dialog.guide.submodule_remove.step2: Its folder and its .gitmodules entry are removed and staged.
dialog.guide.submodule_remove.step3: Its stored copy inside .git is deleted, so anything not pushed from it is lost.
dialog.guide.submodule_remove.step4: Commit the change to remove the submodule for everyone.
dialog.guide.worktree_add.step1: A worktree is another folder with its own checked-out branch, sharing this repository's history.
dialog.guide.worktree_add.step2: A branch can be checked out in only one worktree at a time, so a new branch is often easiest.
dialog.guide.worktree_add.step3: Commits made in either folder show up in both straight away.
dialog.guide.worktree_add.step4: Remove the worktree when you are done; its branch and commits stay.
dialog.guide.worktree_lock.step1: Lock a worktree that lives on a removable drive or network share that is not always there.
dialog.guide.worktree_lock.step2: While it is locked, Git won't prune, move or remove it.
dialog.guide.worktree_lock.step3: The reason is shown to anyone who tries; unlock it when it is no longer needed.
dialog.guide.worktree_move.step1: The worktree's folder moves to the new place, with all its files.
dialog.guide.worktree_move.step2: Git updates its records, so the worktree keeps its branch and history.
dialog.guide.worktree_move.step3: The main worktree, and worktrees that contain submodules, can't be moved this way.
dialog.guide.worktree_remove.step1: The worktree's folder is deleted, with everything in it.
dialog.guide.worktree_remove.step2: A worktree with changes or untracked files is removed only with force, and those changes are lost.
dialog.guide.worktree_remove.step3: Its branch and commits stay unless you choose to delete the branch.
